tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

     6

Exit code 1
Your mission

Build an AI-powered application that ingests heterogeneous data, derives customer requirements for a vehicle, prioritizes them, and puts a product manager in the loop at the decisions that matter.

Your app should be able to:
•    Ingest the provided data and enrich it with structured knowledge from the web.
•    Extract signals such as recurring complaints, unmet needs, competitor advantages and market trends, each linked to its sources.
•    Derive requirements from those findings: clear, actionable, customer-facing and realistic.
•    Prioritize them with a logic you define and can explain.
•    Involve the PM to approve, reject, edit or challenge requirements and their rationale and evidence behind them.
•    Record everything in an audit trail (is a complete, chronological record of all actions, changes, and access events within a system or data environment).


About the Scope

In scope:
•    Customer requirements on the product: features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services, design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as experienced by the customer, variant and package offering, etc.

Out of scope:
•    Regulatory and homologation requirements (e.g.: safety, emissions, type approval)
•    Technical and engineering requirements (e.g.: component specs, architecture, supplier topics)
•    Pricing, business case and cost calculation (you may use cost or effort as a rough prioritization factor)


Make it yours!

Demonstrate your application at least for one derivative in onbe market but avoid designing it as a one-off: it should be adaptable to other BMW vehicles and markets. The remaining datasets and scenarios are available for optional testing.
We know the challenge is broad. Focus on the parts where your team can make the strongest contribution. You might go deep on web research and turn external information into usable evidence, or on integrating and interpreting the provided BMW data. You do not need to develop every capability to the same depth. Be creative, but show how your chosen focus connects to the overall path from evidence to a PM decision.
![data_and_source.png](data_and_source.png)


Expected Deliverables

A concept and demonstrable prototype of an AI-powered product requirements application that processes heterogeneous inputs, derives product requirements, supports prioritization, and integrates human review.

A structured sample list of derived product requirements. Each requirement should include a unique identifier, a clear and actionable description, its linked findings and sources, a priority or score, the applied prioritization rationale, an evidence level, the key future-facing assumptions and uncertainties and its current decision status.

A clearly defined end-to-end workflow showing how inputs are processed into proposed and prioritized requirements, which activities the AI performs autonomously, and where human review is mandatory.

A demonstrable audit trail that makes each requirement traceable from its underlying findings and sources through consolidation, scoring, prioritization, and human decision-making. It should record relevant changes to requirement content, scores, priorities, evidence, and status, including who or what initiated each change, when it occurred, and the documented rationale.

Important: Teams are free to choose their technical approach, architecture, prioritization logic, and user experience. The deliverables describe the capabilities and outcomes that should be demonstrated, not a prescribed solution design. Deliverables may be presented as one integrated solution or as a combination of connected concepts, prototypes, models, and visualizations.

342	     1	# Requirement Model, Evidence Levels & Prioritization
343	     2	
344	     3	**Status: DRAFT v3** (adds per-market scoring D-011, future needs D-012, continuous re-prioritization D-013) — prioritization weights still open (Q-004).
345	     4	
346	     5	## Requirement fields (all required by BMW deliverable + our additions)
347	     6	
348	     7	| Field | Notes |
349	     8	|---|---|
350	     9	| `id` | Global `REQ-0001`, stable forever |
351	    10	| `targets` | One or more (derivative × market) with realization type: `carry_over`, `platform_wide`, `derivative_specific`, `market_variant`, `package`. **Each target has its own score, priority and fit result** (D-011) |
352	    11	| `horizon` | `today` (fix/keep) or `at_successor_launch` (projected 3–5 yr need) (D-012) |
353	    12	| `kano_class` / `kano_drift` | basic / performance / delighter, and expected drift by SOP (e.g. delighter → basic) |
354	    13	| `title` / `description` | Customer-facing, actionable, solution-neutral where possible |
355	    14	| `category` | Exterior · Interior · Comfort & Space · Infotainment & Digital · Driving Experience · Range & Charging · Variants & Packages · Design & Quality Perception |
356	    15	| `target_metric` / `acceptance_criteria` | Measurable where possible |
357	    16	| `linked_findings` → sources | Every requirement ≥ 1 finding; every finding ≥ 1 source |
358	    17	| `fit_checks` | brand / segment / market / feasibility per target — pass / warn / fail + rationale |
359	    18	| `score`, `score_breakdown`, `priority` | Per target; Must / Should / Could from score + PM decision; full history via `score_snapshot` |
360	    19	| `rationale` | Plain-language explanation of score |
361	    20	| `evidence_level` | See below |
362	    21	| `assumptions` / `uncertainties` | Forward-looking (3–5 yr) beliefs and what could make them wrong |
363	    22	| `conflicting_evidence` | Contradicting sources — shown, not hidden |
364	    23	| `status` | `proposed` → `in_review` → `approved` / `rejected` / `deferred`; `challenged` loops back |
365	    24	
366	    25	## Evidence levels
367	    26	
368	    27	| Level | Meaning |
369	    28	|---|---|
370	    29	| **E1 Strong** | Multiple independent T1 sources agree (verbatims across sources + study gap and/or sales signal) |
371	    30	| **E2 Moderate** | One strong T1 source, or T1 + T2 |
372	    31	| **E3 Weak** | Few verbatims or external-only (T2/T3) |
373	    32	| **E4 Assumption** | Forward-looking trend/expectation without current customer evidence |
374	    33	
375	    34	## Gates (before scoring counts)
376	    35	
377	    36	- **Brand fit = fail** → requirement cannot be approved for that target without a PM override + rationale.
378	    37	- **Feasibility = fail** (no platform/plant can deliver it for that market in time) → same.
379	    38	- `warn` results lower the score via the confidence factor and are shown prominently.
380	    39	
381	    40	## Prioritization (draft, explainable weighted score 0–100)
382	    41	
383	    42	| Factor | Signal | Default weight |
384	    43	|---|---|---|
385	    44	| Customer pain / desire | dedup'd verbatim frequency, share of segment, severity (Defect/DTU > Want) | 25 |
386	    45	| Satisfaction gap | low study score / bottom-box vs. other models & categories | 15 |
387	    46	| Market volume & momentum | sales volume of this derivative × market, 2030 growth, share under pressure (e.g. China) | 15 |
388	    47	| Market-profile fit | how strongly climate, usage and culture of this market amplify the need (e.g. rear-seat comfort in CN chauffeur use, seat ventilation in hot climates) | modifier ±10 |
389	    48	| Competitive pressure | competitors in segment × market offer it / reviews cite it | 15 |
390	    49	| Portfolio leverage | number of derivatives/markets benefiting on same platform (carry-over) | 10 |
391	    50	| Future relevance | trend strength 3–5 yr, Kano drift, NK timing | 10 |
392	    51	| Evidence freshness | decay on old evidence unless re-confirmed (D-013) | multiplier 0.7–1.0 |
393	    52	| Brand & segment fit | strength of fit (pass strong / pass / warn) | 10 |
394	    53	| Evidence confidence | multiplier by evidence level | ×(1.0 / 0.85 / 0.7 / 0.5) |
395	    54	| Rough effort (optional) | S/M/L penalty (carry-over cheaper than derivative-specific) | −0…10 |
396	    55	
397	    56	Plus **"must not lose" flag** for strong delighters (Likes).
398	    57	
399	    58	PM can change weights in the UI; each change creates a new `weights_version`, an audit event and a prioritization run with a visible diff.
400	    59	
401	    60	## Continuous re-prioritization (D-013)
402	    61	
403	    62	- Every prioritization run snapshots score, breakdown, rank and priority per requirement-target.
404	    63	- Scores may be recomputed automatically (logged); **priority and status changes are only proposed** (`change_proposal`) and need a PM decision.
405	    64	- Each proposal states its cause: which new evidence, weight change, or market shift moved it, and by how much per factor.
406	    65	- The PM sees a priority timeline per requirement and a "what changed since last run" view.

408	     1	# Knowledge Base & Web Enrichment
409	     2	
410	     3	**Status: DRAFT (D-007).** BMW's own customer data is not enough. The knowledge base combines internal data, curated reference data and web evidence.
411	     4	
412	     5	## Three layers
413	     6	
414	     7	| Layer | Contents | How it gets in | Changes |
415	     8	|---|---|---|---|
416	     9	| **1. BMW internal** | Verbatims, customer studies, sales volumes, option lists (`data-inventory.md`) | Deterministic loaders | Read-only |
417	    10	| **2. Curated reference** | Platforms, plants (location, platforms, powertrains, NK readiness), production allocation, brand positioning + guardrails, segments, competitor model catalog | Research agents propose → human accepts | Versioned; every fact has source + date |
418	    11	| **3. Web evidence** | Competitor features & sales, market demand & powertrain trends, professional reviews, customer expectation studies, owner forums/social | Research agents, on demand or scheduled | Append-only, timestamped |
419	    12	
420	    13	Seed docs: `portfolio-reference.md` (platforms, plants, BMW sales), `competitor-landscape.md` (competitors, trends, brand positioning).
421	    14	
422	    15	## Research agents (OpenAI web search; orchestration framework open — Q-014)
423	    16	
424	    17	| Agent | Question it answers | Typical sources |
425	    18	|---|---|---|
426	    19	| **Competitor scout** | Who competes per segment × market, what they offer that BMW doesn't | OEM sites, press releases, reviews |
427	    20	| **Market & sales analyst** | Volumes and growth by brand/model/powertrain/market; which models are in demand | ACEA, KBA, CPCA, Cox/Automotive News, OEM reports |
428	    21	| **Review miner** | What professional reviewers and owners praise/criticize (BMW + competitors) | Car and Driver, Autocar, Auto Bild, Autohome/Dongchedi, forums |
429	    22	| **Trend & expectation scout** | Customer expectations 3–5 years ahead (software, ADAS, charging, interior, personalization) | J.D. Power, McKinsey, Deloitte, S&P |
430	    23	| **Brand-fit checker** | Does a requirement fit BMW brand + the derivative's segment? | Brand reference (layer 2) |
431	    24	| **Feasibility checker** | Can the target platform/plant build it for that market at the planned time? | Platform/plant reference (layer 2) |
432	    25	
433	    26	Each agent returns **structured output** (Pydantic schema): claim, quote, URL, publisher, published date, retrieved date, market, model(s), trust tier. Free-text LLM opinions are **never** stored as sources.
434	    27	
435	    28	## Trust tiers
436	    29	
437	    30	| Tier | Examples | Default weight |
438	    31	|---|---|---|
439	    32	| **T1** | BMW internal data; official OEM press/annual reports; registration statistics (KBA, ACEA, CPCA) | 1.0 |
440	    33	| **T2** | Reputable press & analysts (Reuters, Bloomberg, Automotive News, J.D. Power, McKinsey), professional reviews | 0.8 |
441	    34	| **T3** | Forums, social media, blogs, aggregators | 0.5 |
442	    35	
443	    36	Rules: prefer recent sources (flag > 24 months old); when sources disagree, store both and raise `conflicting_evidence`; facts the user supplied are stored as `T3/user-claim` until verified.
444	    37	
445	    38	## Brand & segment fit (D-008)
446	    39	
447	    40	Every requirement is checked against the brand profile (BMW: driving pleasure, sportiness, driver focus, premium quality, design, innovation) and the derivative's segment. Example: a "budget, efficiency-first family hatch" spec contradicts BMW positioning → `fail`, regardless of how loudly a generic market trend demands it. Guardrails live in `brand.guardrails_json`, seeded from `competitor-landscape.md`.
448	    41	
449	    42	## Platform & plant feasibility (D-009)
450	    43	
451	    44	For each `requirement_target`: is the derivative's platform (and its successor, e.g. NK) able to carry the requirement; does a plant that builds this platform + powertrain serve that market; is the timing compatible with NK rollout? Output `pass / warn / fail` + rationale. This is a **feasibility filter on customer requirements**, not an engineering spec (scope stays customer-facing).

=== challenge-brief
     1	# Challenge Brief — BMW "AI for Product Decision Making"
     2	
     3	Source: `challange information document/BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf`, `mission.md`, `image_1.png`, `image_2.png`, `data_and_source.png`.
     4	
     5	## The question
     6	
     7	> What should the next generation of a BMW vehicle offer its customers?
     8	
     9	Build an AI-powered app that helps **product managers (PMs)** derive, justify and prioritize **customer requirements** for a **successor vehicle**, grounded in customer feedback, BMW product + sales data, and web research — with the **PM firmly in control of every decision**.
    10	
    11	- Vehicles: BMW **1 Series (F70)**, **5 Series (G60, China LWB = G68)**, **7 Series (G70)** — any one or a combination.
    12	- Markets: **Europe, China, US** — any subset.
    13	- Horizon: **3–5 years ahead** (needs at successor launch, not just today).
    14	- Definition: **Customer Requirement = Customer-relevant attribute of a car.**
    15	- Must make clear **what is evidence vs. forward-looking assumption**.
    16	
    17	## The app must be able to
    18	
    19	1. **Ingest** provided data and **enrich** with structured web knowledge.
    20	2. **Extract signals** — recurring complaints, unmet needs, competitor advantages, market trends — **each linked to sources**.
    21	3. **Derive requirements** — clear, actionable, customer-facing, realistic.
    22	4. **Prioritize** — with a logic we define and can explain.
    23	5. **Involve the PM** — approve, reject, edit, or challenge requirements, rationale and evidence.
    24	6. **Audit trail** — complete chronological record of all actions, changes, access events.
    25	
    26	## Scope
    27	
    28	**In:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment & digital services, design & quality perception, driving experience, range & charging *as experienced by the customer*, variant & package offering.
    29	
    30	**Out:** regulatory/homologation (safety, emissions, type approval); technical/engineering (component specs, architecture, suppliers); pricing / business case / cost calculation (rough cost/effort as a prioritization factor is OK).
    31	
    32	## Expected deliverables (checklist)
    33	
    34	- [ ] **Concept + demonstrable prototype** — heterogeneous inputs → derived requirements → prioritization → human review.
    35	- [ ] **Structured sample requirement list**. Each requirement has:
    36	  - [ ] unique ID
    37	  - [ ] clear, actionable description
    38	  - [ ] linked findings and sources
    39	  - [ ] priority / score
    40	  - [ ] applied prioritization rationale
    41	  - [ ] evidence level
    42	  - [ ] key future-facing assumptions & uncertainties
    43	  - [ ] current decision status
    44	- [ ] **End-to-end workflow definition** — what AI does autonomously, where human review is mandatory.
    45	- [ ] **Demonstrable audit trail** — requirement traceable from sources → findings → consolidation → scoring → prioritization → human decision; records changes to content, scores, priorities, evidence, status, with **who/what**, **when**, **rationale**.
    46	
    47	## BMW's reference process (image_2.png)
    48	
    49	1. **Situation analysis** — baseline (previous BMW model, BMW portfolio, sales volume) + competition, customer/public feedback, product & global trends. (AI + human)
    50	2. **Structure & context** — AI standardizes findings, identifies duplicates, groups themes, connects insights → list of all potential requirements (0/1: implement?).
    51	3. **Requirements definition** — specification & quantification: measurable targets + acceptance criteria (e.g. "Range: 600 or 700 mi?", "Cooler for how many bottles?"), grouped by Exterior / Interior / Powertrain / Driver assistance / … (AI + human)
    52	4. **Prioritization** — Customer, Business, … dimensions. (AI + human)
    53	5. **Documentation** — requirements tracking. (AI)
    54	
    55	## Judging signals (what BMW says it values)
    56	
    57	- Trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning.
    58	- Thoughtful prioritization.
    59	- Clear handling of **uncertainty and conflicting evidence**.
    60	- Customer value over engineering specs / regulation / business case.
    61	- **Scalability** across vehicle lines, markets, future decisions → **don't build a one-off**.
    62	- Focus is free: go deep where we're strongest, but show how it connects to the full path evidence → PM decision.
    63	
    64	## BMW mentor clarifications (Discord, 2026-10-10)
    65	
    66	Common PM pain points, straight from BMW:
    67	
    68	1. **Balancing customer requirements across markets/regions.** Preferences differ by **climate, real-world usage and culture** — what works in one market can fail in another. → Never treat "the customer" as one group (D-011).
    69	2. **Getting early customer feedback and extracting *future* requirements**, e.g. from feedback on predecessor vehicles. → Project what customers will want at successor launch, not just what they complained about (D-012).
    70	3. **The requirements process is ongoing (~2 years), not a one-time list.** The most relevant requirements are re-prioritized again and again. → Continuous re-prioritization with history, so the PM sees how and why priorities changed (D-013).

=== architecture
     1	# Architecture & Workflow
     2	
     3	**Status: DRAFT v3 — conceptual.** The workflow, entities and rules below are the agreed *concept* (D-005, D-008–D-013). The *technical* architecture (orchestration framework, storage, vector DB, graph, RAG) is **not decided** — see Q-014. The data model is a logical model, not a storage decision.
     4	
     5	## Guiding principle
     6	
     7	BMW decides at **portfolio level** — across shared platforms (CLAR, FAAR, Neue Klasse), plants and markets — not one car at a time. The data model is therefore **multi-brand, multi-derivative, multi-market, platform- and plant-aware from day one**. The 5 Series (G60 + China LWB G68) is the deepest worked example; F70 and G70 run through the same pipeline.
     8	
     9	## End-to-end workflow
    10	
    11	| # | Stage | Actor | Output |
    12	|---|---|---|---|
    13	| 1 | **Ingest** BMW data (feedback, study, sales, option lists) for all derivatives × markets | AI (autonomous) | `source_item` with provenance (file, sheet, row) and scope (derivative, market) |
    14	| 2 | **Load reference data** — platforms, plants, brand positioning, segments, competitor models | AI-researched, **human-curated** | reference tables, each fact with source + date (`portfolio-reference.md`, `competitor-landscape.md` are the seeds) |
    15	| 3 | **Enrich via web research agents** — competitors, sales, demand, reviews, trends, customer expectations (see `knowledge-base.md`) | AI (autonomous), PM can accept/reject sources | `source_item(kind=web)` with URL, date, publisher, trust tier, quote |
    16	| 4 | **Extract signals** — classify, dedupe, cluster into findings: complaint / unmet need / must-not-lose delighter / competitor advantage / market trend / brand expectation | AI (autonomous) | `finding` with scope (derivative / platform / market / portfolio), linked sources, metrics |
    17	| 5 | **Derive requirements** — customer-facing, actionable, measurable target + acceptance criteria; scoped to one or more derivatives × markets | AI proposes | `requirement` (status `proposed`) + `requirement_target` rows |
    18	| 6 | **Fit & feasibility checks** per target (D-008, D-009): brand fit, segment fit, market fit, platform/plant feasibility | AI checks, flags explained | `fit_check` rows: pass / warn / fail + rationale + evidence |
    19	| 7 | **Score & prioritize** — explainable factors incl. market volume and portfolio leverage (`requirement-model.md`) | AI computes, PM adjusts weights | score breakdown + rationale |
    20	| 8 | **PM review** — approve / reject / edit / challenge / defer; override failed checks only with rationale | **Human (mandatory)** | status change + rationale |
    21	| 9 | **Document & export** — requirement list, portfolio view, full audit trail | AI | JSON / XLSX export, audit timeline per requirement |
    22	
    23	### It's a loop, not a one-shot (D-013)
    24	
    25	The requirements process runs **~2 years**. Steps 1–9 repeat whenever something changes:
    26	
    27	```
    28	new ingest batch (feedback wave, study, sales update, competitor launch, web refresh)
    29	  → re-extract / update findings (only affected ones)
    30	  → future-need projection refresh
    31	  → prioritization run (snapshot of all requirement-target scores & ranks)
    32	  → change proposals (priority/status/content) → PM accepts/rejects
    33	  → history: priority timeline per requirement with the "why" of each move
    34	```
    35	
    36	Triggers: `new_evidence`, `weight_change`, `pm_request`, `scheduled`. Evidence has a freshness decay; stale evidence loses weight unless re-confirmed.
    37	
    38	### Markets are distinct customer groups (D-011)
    39	
    40	Findings are segmented by market; every requirement-target (derivative × market) has its **own** score, priority and fit result. A `market_profile` (climate, usage, culture, infrastructure) feeds extraction, projection and fit checks. Cross-market conflicts are flagged with realization options (global / market variant / package).
    41	
    42	### Future needs (D-012)
    43	
    44	Step 5 includes **future-need projection**: predecessor findings + competitor trajectory + trends + market profile → need at successor SOP, with horizon (`today` / `at_successor_launch`) and Kano class + expected drift.
    45	
    46	**Mandatory human gates:** final status of every requirement; overriding a failed brand-fit or feasibility check; accepting curated reference data (platform/plant facts). Optional gates: accepting web sources, merging/splitting findings, changing weights.
    47	
    48	## Core data model (draft)
    49	
    50	### Reference layer (portfolio)
    51	```
    52	brand(id, name, group, positioning, core_values[], guardrails_json, source_ids[])
    53	segment(id, name, e.g. premium_compact | upper_mid | luxury, description)
    54	platform(id e.g. CLAR | FAAR | NK, owner_brand_group, powertrains_supported[], introduced, phase_out, successor_platform_id, source_ids[])
    55	vehicle_model(id e.g. G60, brand_id, line "5 Series", body, segment_id, platform_id, generation,
    56	              sop, eop_planned, powertrains[], is_bmw_group, market_variants[])   -- BMW + competitors in one table
    57	market(code EU | US | CN | RoW, countries[])
    58	market_profile(market_code, climate, usage_patterns, cultural_expectations, infrastructure, powertrain_mix, source_ids[], valid_from)
    59	plant(id, name, city, country, platforms_supported[], powertrains_supported[], nk_ready_from, capacity_note, source_ids[])
    60	production(vehicle_model_id, plant_id, market_variant e.g. "G68 LWB", markets_served[], since, until)
    61	sales(vehicle_model_id, market_code, year, units, is_forecast, source_id)
    62	```
    63	
    64	### Evidence layer
    65	```
    66	source_item(id, kind[feedback|study|sales|option_list|web|reference], trust_tier[T1..T3],
    67	            vehicle_model_id?, market_code?, platform_id?, ref, url?, published_at?, retrieved_at,
    68	            text, quote, meta_json)
    69	finding(id, type, title, summary, scope_level[derivative|platform|market|portfolio],
    70	        metrics_json, created_by, created_at)
    71	finding_scope(finding_id, vehicle_model_id?, market_code?, platform_id?)
    72	finding_source(finding_id, source_item_id, quote, relation[supports|contradicts])
    73	```
    74	
    75	### Decision layer
    76	```
    77	requirement(id "REQ-0001", title, description, category, target_metric, acceptance_criteria,
    78	            horizon[today|at_successor_launch], kano_class[basic|performance|delighter], kano_drift,
    79	            evidence_level, assumptions, uncertainties, conflicting_evidence,
    80	            status, version)                                   -- content versioned; old versions kept
    81	requirement_target(requirement_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code,
    82	                   realization[carry_over|platform_wide|derivative_specific|market_variant|package],
    83	                   score, score_breakdown_json, priority, rationale)   -- per-market priority (D-011)
    84	requirement_finding(requirement_id, finding_id, relation[supports|contradicts])
    85	fit_check(id, requirement_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code, check[brand|segment|market|feasibility],
    86	          result[pass|warn|fail], rationale, evidence_source_ids[], checked_by, checked_at)
    87	audit_event(id, ts, actor_type[ai|human|system], actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id,
    88	            field, old_value, new_value, rationale, model, prompt_ref)   -- append-only
    89	```
    90	
    91	### Continuity layer (D-013)
    92	```
    93	ingest_batch(id, ts, kind[feedback_wave|study|sales|competitor_event|web_refresh], description, source_ids[])
    94	prioritization_run(id, ts, trigger[new_evidence|weight_change|pm_request|scheduled], ingest_batch_id?,
    95	                   weights_version, model, initiated_by)
    96	score_snapshot(run_id, requirement_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code, score, breakdown_json, rank, priority)
    97	change_proposal(id, run_id, requirement_id, target?, field, old_value, proposed_value, reason,
    98	                evidence_delta_json, status[open|accepted|rejected], decided_by, decided_at, decision_rationale)
    99	weights_version(id, weights_json, created_by, created_at, rationale)
   100	llm_usage(id, ts, job, model, input_tokens, cached_tokens, output_tokens, search_calls, cost_usd)   -- budget tracking (D-010)
   101	```
   102	
   103	Requirement IDs are global (`REQ-0001`); scope lives in `requirement_target`, so one requirement can apply to several derivatives/markets (e.g. an infotainment UX fix across all CLAR cars).
   104	
   105	## Audit trail rules
   106	
   107	- Append-only: no UPDATE/DELETE on `audit_event`.
   108	- Every mutation of requirement content, targets, score, priority, evidence links, fit checks or status → one event (who/what, when, before/after, rationale).
   109	- AI events record model name + prompt/agent version; web research events record queries and URLs.
   110	- Access events (view/export) logged as well.
   111	
   112	## Key UI views (planned)
   113	
   114	- **Portfolio matrix** — derivatives × markets, with platform and plant, sales trend, top findings, requirement count.
   115	- **Requirement detail** — evidence chain (sources → findings → requirement), fit checks, score breakdown, audit timeline, approve/reject/edit/challenge.
   116	- **Competitor view** — per segment × market: who sells what, strengths, gaps vs. BMW.
   117	- **Ranked backlog** — per market (EU / US / CN side by side), adjustable weights, visible re-ranking diff.
   118	- **Priority history** — timeline per requirement across prioritization runs, each move annotated with its cause (new evidence, weight change, PM decision).
   119	- **Change inbox** — open AI change proposals after a new ingest batch; PM accepts/rejects with rationale.
   120	- **Market conflict view** — requirements whose priority diverges strongly between markets, with realization options.
=== requirement-model
     1	# Requirement Model, Evidence Levels & Prioritization
     2	
     3	**Status: DRAFT v3** (adds per-market scoring D-011, future needs D-012, continuous re-prioritization D-013) — prioritization weights still open (Q-004).
     4	
     5	## Requirement fields (all required by BMW deliverable + our additions)
     6	
     7	| Field | Notes |
     8	|---|---|
     9	| `id` | Global `REQ-0001`, stable forever |
    10	| `targets` | One or more (derivative × market) with realization type: `carry_over`, `platform_wide`, `derivative_specific`, `market_variant`, `package`. **Each target has its own score, priority and fit result** (D-011) |
    11	| `horizon` | `today` (fix/keep) or `at_successor_launch` (projected 3–5 yr need) (D-012) |
    12	| `kano_class` / `kano_drift` | basic / performance / delighter, and expected drift by SOP (e.g. delighter → basic) |
    13	| `title` / `description` | Customer-facing, actionable, solution-neutral where possible |
    14	| `category` | Exterior · Interior · Comfort & Space · Infotainment & Digital · Driving Experience · Range & Charging · Variants & Packages · Design & Quality Perception |
    15	| `target_metric` / `acceptance_criteria` | Measurable where possible |
    16	| `linked_findings` → sources | Every requirement ≥ 1 finding; every finding ≥ 1 source |
    17	| `fit_checks` | brand / segment / market / feasibility per target — pass / warn / fail + rationale |
    18	| `score`, `score_breakdown`, `priority` | Per target; Must / Should / Could from score + PM decision; full history via `score_snapshot` |
    19	| `rationale` | Plain-language explanation of score |
    20	| `evidence_level` | See below |
    21	| `assumptions` / `uncertainties` | Forward-looking (3–5 yr) beliefs and what could make them wrong |
    22	| `conflicting_evidence` | Contradicting sources — shown, not hidden |
    23	| `status` | `proposed` → `in_review` → `approved` / `rejected` / `deferred`; `challenged` loops back |
    24	
    25	## Evidence levels
    26	
    27	| Level | Meaning |
    28	|---|---|
    29	| **E1 Strong** | Multiple independent T1 sources agree (verbatims across sources + study gap and/or sales signal) |
    30	| **E2 Moderate** | One strong T1 source, or T1 + T2 |
    31	| **E3 Weak** | Few verbatims or external-only (T2/T3) |
    32	| **E4 Assumption** | Forward-looking trend/expectation without current customer evidence |
    33	
    34	## Gates (before scoring counts)
    35	
    36	- **Brand fit = fail** → requirement cannot be approved for that target without a PM override + rationale.
    37	- **Feasibility = fail** (no platform/plant can deliver it for that market in time) → same.
    38	- `warn` results lower the score via the confidence factor and are shown prominently.
    39	
    40	## Prioritization (draft, explainable weighted score 0–100)
    41	
    42	| Factor | Signal | Default weight |
    43	|---|---|---|
    44	| Customer pain / desire | dedup'd verbatim frequency, share of segment, severity (Defect/DTU > Want) | 25 |
    45	| Satisfaction gap | low study score / bottom-box vs. other models & categories | 15 |
    46	| Market volume & momentum | sales volume of this derivative × market, 2030 growth, share under pressure (e.g. China) | 15 |
    47	| Market-profile fit | how strongly climate, usage and culture of this market amplify the need (e.g. rear-seat comfort in CN chauffeur use, seat ventilation in hot climates) | modifier ±10 |
    48	| Competitive pressure | competitors in segment × market offer it / reviews cite it | 15 |
    49	| Portfolio leverage | number of derivatives/markets benefiting on same platform (carry-over) | 10 |
    50	| Future relevance | trend strength 3–5 yr, Kano drift, NK timing | 10 |
    51	| Evidence freshness | decay on old evidence unless re-confirmed (D-013) | multiplier 0.7–1.0 |
    52	| Brand & segment fit | strength of fit (pass strong / pass / warn) | 10 |
    53	| Evidence confidence | multiplier by evidence level | ×(1.0 / 0.85 / 0.7 / 0.5) |
    54	| Rough effort (optional) | S/M/L penalty (carry-over cheaper than derivative-specific) | −0…10 |
    55	
    56	Plus **"must not lose" flag** for strong delighters (Likes).
    57	
    58	PM can change weights in the UI; each change creates a new `weights_version`, an audit event and a prioritization run with a visible diff.
    59	
    60	## Continuous re-prioritization (D-013)
    61	
    62	- Every prioritization run snapshots score, breakdown, rank and priority per requirement-target.
    63	- Scores may be recomputed automatically (logged); **priority and status changes are only proposed** (`change_proposal`) and need a PM decision.
    64	- Each proposal states its cause: which new evidence, weight change, or market shift moved it, and by how much per factor.
    65	- The PM sees a priority timeline per requirement and a "what changed since last run" view.
=== knowledge-base
     1	# Knowledge Base & Web Enrichment
     2	
     3	**Status: DRAFT (D-007).** BMW's own customer data is not enough. The knowledge base combines internal data, curated reference data and web evidence.
     4	
     5	## Three layers
     6	
     7	| Layer | Contents | How it gets in | Changes |
     8	|---|---|---|---|
     9	| **1. BMW internal** | Verbatims, customer studies, sales volumes, option lists (`data-inventory.md`) | Deterministic loaders | Read-only |
    10	| **2. Curated reference** | Platforms, plants (location, platforms, powertrains, NK readiness), production allocation, brand positioning + guardrails, segments, competitor model catalog | Research agents propose → human accepts | Versioned; every fact has source + date |
    11	| **3. Web evidence** | Competitor features & sales, market demand & powertrain trends, professional reviews, customer expectation studies, owner forums/social | Research agents, on demand or scheduled | Append-only, timestamped |
    12	
    13	Seed docs: `portfolio-reference.md` (platforms, plants, BMW sales), `competitor-landscape.md` (competitors, trends, brand positioning).
    14	
    15	## Research agents (OpenAI web search; orchestration framework open — Q-014)
    16	
    17	| Agent | Question it answers | Typical sources |
    18	|---|---|---|
    19	| **Competitor scout** | Who competes per segment × market, what they offer that BMW doesn't | OEM sites, press releases, reviews |
    20	| **Market & sales analyst** | Volumes and growth by brand/model/powertrain/market; which models are in demand | ACEA, KBA, CPCA, Cox/Automotive News, OEM reports |
    21	| **Review miner** | What professional reviewers and owners praise/criticize (BMW + competitors) | Car and Driver, Autocar, Auto Bild, Autohome/Dongchedi, forums |
    22	| **Trend & expectation scout** | Customer expectations 3–5 years ahead (software, ADAS, charging, interior, personalization) | J.D. Power, McKinsey, Deloitte, S&P |
    23	| **Brand-fit checker** | Does a requirement fit BMW brand + the derivative's segment? | Brand reference (layer 2) |
    24	| **Feasibility checker** | Can the target platform/plant build it for that market at the planned time? | Platform/plant reference (layer 2) |
    25	
    26	Each agent returns **structured output** (Pydantic schema): claim, quote, URL, publisher, published date, retrieved date, market, model(s), trust tier. Free-text LLM opinions are **never** stored as sources.
    27	
    28	## Trust tiers
    29	
    30	| Tier | Examples | Default weight |
    31	|---|---|---|
    32	| **T1** | BMW internal data; official OEM press/annual reports; registration statistics (KBA, ACEA, CPCA) | 1.0 |
    33	| **T2** | Reputable press & analysts (Reuters, Bloomberg, Automotive News, J.D. Power, McKinsey), professional reviews | 0.8 |
    34	| **T3** | Forums, social media, blogs, aggregators | 0.5 |
    35	
    36	Rules: prefer recent sources (flag > 24 months old); when sources disagree, store both and raise `conflicting_evidence`; facts the user supplied are stored as `T3/user-claim` until verified.
    37	
    38	## Brand & segment fit (D-008)
    39	
    40	Every requirement is checked against the brand profile (BMW: driving pleasure, sportiness, driver focus, premium quality, design, innovation) and the derivative's segment. Example: a "budget, efficiency-first family hatch" spec contradicts BMW positioning → `fail`, regardless of how loudly a generic market trend demands it. Guardrails live in `brand.guardrails_json`, seeded from `competitor-landscape.md`.
    41	
    42	## Platform & plant feasibility (D-009)
    43	
    44	For each `requirement_target`: is the derivative's platform (and its successor, e.g. NK) able to carry the requirement; does a plant that builds this platform + powertrain serve that market; is the timing compatible with NK rollout? Output `pass / warn / fail` + rationale. This is a **feasibility filter on customer requirements**, not an engineering spec (scope stays customer-facing).

2	     1	# BMW Group Portfolio Reference: Platforms, Plants, Sales
3	     2	
4	     3	Researched on 2026-10-10. Every fact has a source and a publication date in the table rows or in the source list (S#) at the end.
5	     4	
6	     5	Reliability tiers:
7	     6	- **[BMW]**: BMW Group press release or BMW plant fact sheet. Highest confidence.
8	     7	- **[Trade]**: reputable auto or trade press, such as bmwblog, electrive, just-auto or CnEVPost.
9	     8	- **[Unverified]**: comes from one secondary source only, from a leak, or from my own inference. Do not quote it as fact.
10	     9	
11	    10	Q3 2026 delivery figures were not yet published on the research date. BMW usually releases them in mid-October.
12	    11	
13	    12	---
14	    13	
15	    14	## 1. Platforms
16	    15	
17	    16	BMW rarely names its platforms in official press releases. Most platform-to-model mappings below therefore rest on trade press. Plant assignments rest on BMW sources.
18	    17	
19	    18	### 1.1 Current architectures and models
20	    19

China-only BEV i3), 4 Series G22/G23/G26 + i4, 5 Series G60 / Touring G61 / China LWB G68 (incl. i5), 7 Series G70 + i7, 8 Series G14/15/16, X3 G45, China LWB X3, X4 G02 (ended Nov 2025), X5 G05, China LWB X5 G18, X6 G06, X7 G07, XM G09, Z4 G29 (ended 2026), 2 Series Coupé G42 / M2 G87, iX I20 (derivative) | [Trade] S20, S21. Codes are widely used but BMW press does not label them as "CLAR" |
24	    23	| **FAAR** (successor to UKL2) | FWD/AWD, multi-energy | 1 Series F70, 2 Series Gran Coupé F74, 2 Series Active Tourer U06, X1 U11 + iX1, X2 U10 + iX2, China LWB X1/iX1, MINI Countryman U25 (ICE + BEV) | [Trade] S22, S23. **Conflict:** Wikipedia describes F70 as "UKL2", while bmwblog and others call it FAAR (an evolution of UKL). CnEVPost (S19) calls the China iX1 "CLAR", which is almost certainly wrong |

BEV-first, but the 8th-gen 3 Series also brings NK design and tech to ICE derivatives | iX3 NA5 (since Oct 2025), i3 sedan NA0 (since Aug 2026); planned: iX3 LWB NA6 (China), i3 Touring NA1, iX4 NA7, i4 Coupé/Convertible NA2/NA3, i7 successor ND0, i1 NB0 (rumoured), NK electric X1 NB5/NB6, NK M cars (ZA0 M3, etc.) | NA5/NA0 and plants [BMW] S7, S9, S10. Codes and future list [Trade] S21 (bmwblog, 12 Dec 2025) |

29	    28	### 1.2 What NK replaces, and when
30	    29	
31	    30	- BMW says NK technology goes into **"40 new models and model updates" by 2027** [BMW] S7 (17 Sep 2025). BMW's design chief says every model will get NK design/tech [Trade] S24.
32	    31	- **NK does not fully replace CLAR before roughly 2030.** The next large SUVs stay on an upgraded CLAR: X5/iX5 G65, X6/iX6 G66, X7/iX7 G67. CLAR is expected "well into the second half of the decade" [Trade] S21 (Dec 2025); Autocar on the next X7 [Trade] S24.
33	    32	- **Mid-size BEVs move to NK first.** iX3 NA5 replaces the old CLAR iX3 G08. G08 production in China ended in March 2025 [Trade] S19. i3 NA0 replaces the CLAR electric 3 Series/i4 sedan role [Trade] S21.
34	    33	- **New 3 Series (8th generation, revealed Sep 2026).** The BEV i3 is built in Munich. ICE/PHEV variants are built in Dingolfing, starting with the 320 and M350 petrol models [BMW] S11 (30 Sep 2026). Whether the ICE 3 Series sits on NK hardware or on a CLAR evolution is **[Unverified]**. BMW says the 8th-gen 3 Series "introduces Neue Klasse design and technologies".
35	    34	- **China.** The China-built CLAR/FAAR BEVs (i3 LWB, i5, iX1) were reported to end production in **July 2026**. The NK iX3 LWB takes over, followed by an NK i3 LWB in early 2027 [Trade] S19 (CnEVPost, 17 Jun 2026, citing "BMW Club"). This is **[Unverified]** by BMW. The i7 was imported to China and discontinued there in June 2026 [Trade] S19.
36	    35	- **FAAR replacement:** no official date. Trade press expects an NK-based electric X1 (NB5/NB6) after the current iX1 cycle, and an i1 (NB0) "toward end of decade" **[Unverified]** S21.

    29	## Core rules
    30	
    31	1. **Raw data is read-only and confidential.** `challange information document/` (typo is the real folder name) is git-ignored — never modify, move or commit it; never send it anywhere except the agreed LLM provider. Derived data goes to git-ignored `data/`.
    32	2. **Stay in scope.** Customer-facing requirements only (features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment/digital, design & quality perception, driving experience, range/charging as experienced, variants/packages). **Out:** regulatory/homologation, engineering/component specs, pricing/business cases (rough effort as a factor is OK).
    33	3. **Traceability is non-negotiable.** Every finding links to ≥1 source item; every requirement links to ≥1 finding. Keep provenance (file, sheet, row/ID, URL + date for web).
    34	4. **Evidence vs. assumption.** Always separate evidence-backed statements from forward-looking assumptions (3–5 yr horizon); surface conflicting evidence instead of hiding it.
    35	5. **The PM decides, never the AI.** AI only creates/edits in `proposed` status; `approved`/`rejected`/`deferred` require a human actor + rationale.
    36	6. **Audit everything, append-only.** Every change to requirement content, score, priority, evidence or status → an `audit_event` (actor human/ai/system, timestamp, before/after, rationale, model for AI).
    37	7. **Portfolio, not one-offs.** Brands, models, markets, platforms and plants are data/config — never hardcode a derivative or market. Requirements can target several derivative × market combinations.
    38	8. **Brand & segment fit.** Every requirement must fit the brand and the segment (no "cheap efficiency hatch" from BMW, no Bugatti family car). Brand-fit `fail` blocks approval unless a PM overrides with rationale.
    39	9. **Plant & platform feasibility.** A recommendation must be buildable: the derivative's platform and a plant that builds it can serve that market in time (incl. Neue Klasse transition). Used as a feasibility filter only — never output engineering specs.
    40	10. **Web evidence is cited evidence.** Competitor, sales, demand and expectation facts come from web research with URL, publish/retrieve date and trust tier (T1–T3). LLM opinions are never stored as sources; unverified user claims stay flagged until verified.
    41	11. **Explainable prioritization.** Every score has a visible factor breakdown and plain-language rationale.
    42	12. **OpenAI for all LLM work**; model names via env (`OPENAI_MODEL_*`). Secrets live in `.env` (git-ignored); commit `.env.example` only.
    43	13. **Markets are different customers.** Climate, usage and culture differ — segment findings by market and score/prioritize each derivative × market separately; surface cross-market conflicts (D-011).
    44	14. **Future, not just past.** Derive what customers will need at successor launch (3–5 yr) from predecessor feedback + competitors + trends; tag horizon, Kano class and assumptions (D-012).
    45	15. **Living process, not a one-shot list.** ~2-year process: every prioritization run is snapshotted; AI only *proposes* priority/status changes with their cause; PM decides; history is always visible (D-013).
    46	16. **$100 OpenAI budget, total.** Cheap model (`gpt-6-luna`) for bulk extraction/classification/summaries; `gpt-6.1-sol` only for reasoning-heavy steps; all calls through the budget-guarded wrapper; Batch API + caching; update the Budget section in `foundation/STATE.md` after paid runs (D-010).
    47	17. **Don't decide architecture alone.** Framework, storage, vector DB, graph and RAG choices (LangChain, LangGraph, …) are discussed with the team first (Q-014). Don't start scaffolding or implementation until the team says so.
    48	18. **Hackathon pace.** Ship a working demo path end-to-end before polishing; prefer simple, cached, deterministic pipelines over clever ones. Don't build what's not needed for the demo.

    54	- No China verbatims exist; US verbatims dominate G60/G70; F70 has no US data.
    55	- Local anaconda Python is broken for pandas — use a `uv` venv (Python 3.12).

    59	Small, descriptive commits; don't commit unless asked. Never commit raw BMW data, `.env`, or local DBs.

  ## OpenAI pricing and capabilities, as of 2026-10-10
  
  All the pages below were reachable. Main sources: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, /api/docs/models/gpt-6-luna, /api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol, /api/docs/guides/batch, /guides/prompt-caching, /guides/tools-web-search and /guides/spend-limits.
  
  ### 1. Do the models exist, and what do they cost?
  All five IDs exist. Prices are per 1M tokens, input / cached input / output, for short context (prompts of 272K tokens or less).
  
  | Model | Standard | Batch | Flex | Notes |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | gpt-6-luna | $0.10 / $0.01 / $0.50 | $0.05 / $0.005 / $0.25 | same as Batch | Long context: $0.20 / $0.02 / $0.75. Cache write $0.125. |
  | gpt-6.1-sol | $2.00 / $0.10 / $10.00 | $1.00 / $0.05 / $5.00 | same as Batch | Long context: $4 / $0.20 / $15. Cache write $2.50. |
  | gpt-6-astra | $10.00 / $1.00 / $50.00 | $5.00 / $0.50 / $25.00 | same as Batch | Long context: $20 / $2 / $75 |
  | gpt-5-mini | $0.25 / $0.025 / $2.00 | $0.125 / $0.0125 / $1.00 | same as Batch | |
  | text-embedding-3-small | $0.02 (input only) | 50% off via Batch (/v1/embeddings is supported) | – | |
  | gpt-5-nano | $0.05 / $0.005 / $0.40 | $0.025 / $0.0025 / $0.20 | same as Batch | Cheapest text model listed |
  | gpt-5.4-nano | $0.20 / $0.02 / $1.25 | – | $0.10 / $0.01 / $0.625 | |
  | gpt-4.1-nano | $0.10 / $0.025 / $0.40 | $0.05 / – / $0.20 | – | |
  | text-embedding-3-large | $0.13 | | | |
  
  - **Long prompts:** over 272K input tokens, the whole request is charged 2x for input and cache and 1.5x for output.
  - **Fast tier:** Priority was renamed "Fast" on 2026-07-30 and costs 2x Standard (luna $0.20 / $0.02 / $1.00; sol $4 / $0.20 / $20). Sol also has an "Ultrafast" tier at 6x Standard.
  - **Regional or FedRAMP endpoints:** add 10%.
  - **Cheaper alternatives:** gpt-6-luna is already about 2.5x cheaper than gpt-5-mini on input and 4x cheaper on output. Only gpt-5-nano is cheaper ($0.05 / $0.40). The page lists no embedding model newer than text-embedding-3-small, which is still the cheapest.
  - **Cache writes:** on GPT-5.6 and later (which includes luna and sol), writing to the cache costs 1.25x the input rate. It is "not an additive fee": each token is billed once, as uncached, cached or cache-write. The minimum cacheable prompt is 1,024 tokens and the cache TTL is 30 minutes (prompt-caching guide).
  
  ### 2. Batch and Flex
  - Batch is 50% off ("Batch requests cost 50% less than synchronous APIs"). The completion window is 24h only, with up to 50k requests and 200 MB per file. Batch has its own rate limits, separate from the per-model ones.
  - **Does it stack with cached input?** No page says so explicitly. However, the Batch tables list cached-input prices that are 50% of the Standard cached rate (luna $0.005, sol $0.05), which implies they stack.
  - Flex exists, costs the same as Batch, and covers luna, sol, astra, gpt-5-mini and the nanos.
  
  ### 3. Web search tool pricing (pricing page, built-in tools table)
  - **`web_search`, all models (current tool):** "$10.00 / 1k calls + Search content tokens billed at model rates."
  - **`web_search_preview`, reasoning models (gpt-5, o-series):** $10.00 / 1k calls plus search content tokens at model rates.
  - **`web_search_preview`, non-reasoning models:** $25.00 / 1k calls, and "Search content tokens are free."
  - **Fixed-block exception:** "For gpt-4o-mini and gpt-4.1-mini with the non-preview web search tool, search content tokens are billed as a fixed block of 8,000 input tokens per call."
  - **What this means for luna and sol:** both pay $10 per 1k calls plus search tokens at their own input rate. For luna that rate is $0.10/M, so search tokens are almost free.
  - **Search context size:** search context is capped at 128k. The search guide says reasoning models search "agentically", running several searches plus `open_page` and `find_in_page` actions. Each search action is billed as a call, so one request can cost several calls. Non-reasoning models run a single search.
  
  ### 4. Capabilities of gpt-6-luna and gpt-6.1-sol (model pages)
  
  | | gpt-6-luna | gpt-6.1-sol |
  |---|---|---|
  | Context window / max input / max output | 1,050,000 / 922,000 / 128,000 | 1,050,000 / 922,000 / 128,000 |
  | Knowledge cutoff | 2026-05-18 | 2026-04-30 |
  | Reasoning effort | none, low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max | low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. `none` and `minimal` are not supported. |
  | Structured Outputs | Supported | Supported |
  | Function calling | Responses API. In Chat Completions only when reasoning_effort is `none`. | Responses API. Chat Completions only without tool calling. |
  | Endpoints | Responses, Chat Completions, Batch | Responses, Chat Completions, Batch |
  | Built-in tools | web_search, file_search, code_interpreter, MCP and others | same |
  | Deprecation | None listed | None listed |
  | Build-tier rate limits | 5k RPM, 2M TPM, 20M batch queue | 5k RPM, 1M TPM |
  
  Other deprecation notices:
  - o4-mini shuts down on 2026-10-23.
  - gpt-4o-search-preview models were shut down on 2026-07-23.
  - The fine-tuning platform is being wound down.
  - Nothing affects luna, sol, gpt-5-mini or text-embedding-3-small.
  
  ### 5. Does the Batch API support web_search?
  Not documented either way. The Batch guide lists `/v1/responses` as a supported endpoint, but neither the Batch guide nor the web-search guide says whether built-in tools such as web_search run in a batch. The pricing page only says the "Batch API [is] not priced separately." Assume it is unsupported or unverified until a 1-request batch has been run to test it.
  
  ### 6. Project-level hard budget limits
  Yes, they exist. The setting is under Project settings, Limits, Spend, "Enforce a hard limit".
  - Once the limit is reached, requests return 429 with `project_spend_limit_exceeded`. Organization-level limits also exist and apply across all projects.
  - Limits are monthly and reset with the next cycle.
  - Spend alerts are separate. They only send a notification and do not block traffic.
  - The guide warns that enforcement is "not instantaneous, so recorded spend can slightly exceed the configured amount."
  - The guide does not say whether Batch jobs or tool-call fees count toward the limit.
  - A secondary source dates the rollout to 2026-07-22. Older community reports (2025 to May 2026) say project limits were only alerts. The current official docs describe real enforcement.
  - Recommendation: set the hard limit below $100 (for example $90) and keep the budget-guarded wrapper in the app.
  
  ### Other notes
  - **Possible model-page error:** the pricing page mentions "GPT-5.6 Sol promotional pricing through at least Nov 21, 2026", which may be a mislabel. The model pages show no promotion for 6.1-sol.
  - **Long-context threshold:** the 272K threshold matters only if prompts get very large. Staying under it keeps base rates.
</agent-message>

content.text:
# Foundation review: findings

**Bottom line:** the foundation is usable, but three problems need fixing before anyone keeps building on it:
- **BMW data is already public on GitHub**, so this is beyond "before any push".
- **The data inventory miscounts the feedback.** It counts spreadsheet rows instead of unique verbatims, so the source/country/powertrain mix and the text lengths are wrong.
- **The budget plan undercounts by roughly 1.5–3×.**

I made no file edits and no commits, built nothing, and made no architecture choices. The only thing I created was a throwaway Python env in the session scratchpad. I checked the data with pandas, read the briefing PDF and the three images directly, and had three read-only agents check the web facts and OpenAI pricing (36 claims in total).

---

## Critical

**C1. Raw BMW verbatims are public on GitHub, through the Entire CLI's checkpoint ref.**
- **Where:** `.entire/settings.json` (`"checkpoints": {"type": "git-refs"}`, `"telemetry": true`).
- **Evidence:** `git ls-remote origin` shows `refs/entire/checkpoints/05/01M4JYRMFNECFSXRVJXKCRFM05` on the public remote. Its `0/full.jsonl` and `0/transcript.jsonl` hold the previous agent's session, including:
  - 18× "Customer stated", 12× "I had a minor problem", and IDs like `G60-0001` (that is, the verbatim text itself);
  - the `volume_2030` sales columns and the `Preisliste` (option price list) content.
- **Possible key leak:** I was blocked from scanning that ref for an `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Atahan should check it himself:

  ```
  ! git show 31f2275979cc441025a3f545e2e3961b9e509140:0/full.jsonl | grep -c 'sk-proj'
  ```

  If the count is above 0, rotate the key.
- **Fix (needs Atahan, and it's irreversible):**
  1. `git push origin --delete refs/entire/checkpoints/05/01M4JYRMFNECFSXRVJXKCRFM05`
  2. Stop Entire pushing checkpoints (or disable it), and set `telemetry: false`.
  3. Ask GitHub Support to purge cached objects.
  4. Consider making the repo private until the end of the hackathon.

**C2. The committed foundation contains BMW-confidential figures, and `main` is already pushed.**
- `git ls-remote` shows `main` = `8c2a85b` on origin, so "before any push" is too late.
- **Where BMW data appears in committed files:**
  - `data-inventory.md:23-27`: row/ID/country/engine counts per file.
  - `data-inventory.md:54-58`: **sales per derivative × market, including the 2030 forecast**. This is the most sensitive item.
  - `data-inventory.md:11,19-21,33`: the internal VFC taxonomy labels, example IDs, and verbatim openings ("Customer stated…", "I had a minor problem with X - DTU").
  - `data-inventory.md:38-48`: the study's category list, scale labels and structure.
  - `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md:15` (Q-005: verbatim phrasing), `:19` (study scales), `:48` (waves by source).
  - `AGENTS.md:52-54`, `DECISIONS.md:106`, `tech-stack.md:13` (dataset sizes/structure).
- **Fix:**
  1. Move `data-inventory.md`'s numbers, labels and snippets into the git-ignored `data/` folder (e.g. `data/inventory-detail.md`).
  2. Keep only abstract statements in git ("feedback has one row per classification; US-heavy; no CN verbatims").
  3. Rewrite history (`git filter-repo` on those paths) and force-push. That is Atahan's call because it's destructive.
- **Briefing material:** `challenge-brief.md` paraphrases BMW's briefing. That's probably fine, but ask the mentors.

**C3. `.gitignore` doesn't ignore `data/`, even though AGENTS.md:31 and D-002 say derived data goes to a "git-ignored `data/`".**
- It also misses `*.sqlite`, `*.sqlite3`, `*.duckdb`, `*-wal`/`*-journal`, vector-store folders, and stray `*.xlsx`/`*.PDF`/`*.csv`/`*.parquet` exports.
- **Fix:** add those entries. Optionally add a pre-commit grep that blocks `Customer stated|G60-\d{4}|volume_2030`.

**C4. Rule 1 is broken by how the team actually works.**
- `AGENTS.md:31` says raw data must never go anywhere except "the agreed LLM provider" (OpenAI).
- But Claude Code sessions (Anthropic), Codex and Entire telemetry all receive raw data. This review sent Anthropic aggregate statistics and short text fragments.
- **Fix:** the team must decide explicitly which coding-agent providers may see raw data, and write that into rule 1.

**C5. `data-inventory.md:23-27` counts rows, not verbatims, against its own dedupe rule (line 30). That skews every mix figure:**

| Claim | Actual (unique IDs) |
|---|---|
| G60 Source A 1,858 | **854** verbatims (21%, not 37%) |
| G60 BEV 1,763 | 1,363 |
| G60 GB 89 | **36** |
| G70 GB 22 | **8**; G70 has ~19 EU verbatims in total, so "few" really means "none" |
| US share | 90% (G60) / 95% (G70) of verbatims |

- **F70 is 32% Japan** (672 of 2,128 verbatims), yet the coverage matrix at `:76` files F70 under EU only. KR (205 for G60) is ignored entirely. Under D-011 these are RoW customers, not EU ones.
- **Fix:** report unique-ID counts and add RoW (JP/KR/AU/CA) to the coverage matrix.

**C6. BMW's sales file conflicts with public data, and nothing in the foundation says so.**
- `sales_volumes.xlsx` has G60_G68 China 2025 = 75k, **up 10%** on 2024.
- Gasgoo/CPCA (confirmed) gives 5 Series China Jan–Nov 2025 = **107,348**, while BMW China overall fell 12.5%.
- All the xlsx values are round thousands, so they look stylized.
- `STATE.md:54` makes model-level volume depend on this file.
- **Fix:** record the conflict in `data-inventory.md` and `portfolio-reference.md` §4, add a Q-0xx for the mentors ("are the volumes illustrative?"), and never let the scoring silently treat them as real.

**C7. D-010's ~$40 estimate is too low.**
- The prices are correct: luna $0.10/$0.01/$0.50 and sol $2/$0.10/$10 are confirmed, and so are Batch at −50%, web search at $10/1k calls, and embeddings at $0.02.
- The undercount comes from three things the estimate leaves out:
  - **Reasoning tokens** are billed as output.
  - **Every requirement fans out per target** (one score and fit check per derivative × market).
  - **One reasoning-model search request triggers several billed search calls.**
- My recompute at `DECISIONS.md:102-114`, with explicit assumptions:

| Workstream | Assumptions | Doc | Recomputed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Classify 10,128 verbatims ×3 | ~55 tok/verbatim, 25 per call, 2k prompt, ~160 out/verbatim incl. reasoning, Batch | $1.5 | **$1.4** ✓ |
| Embeddings ×3 | 1.5M tok | $0.1 | $0.1 ✓ |
| Cluster labels ×3 | 300×(2.1k in / 0.5k out) luna + 50×(3k / 1.5k) sol | $1 | **~$3.5** |
| Web research | luna reasons by default, so each request makes 3–8 billed search calls; ~540 requests × ~4 calls; ~20k content tok/call | $8 | **$8–26** |
| Derivation + projection | 100 reqs × 15k in / 6k out (incl. reasoning) × 3 runs, synchronous / Batch | $12 | **$14–27** |
| Fit checks | 100 reqs × ~4 targets × 4 checks; sol on 10–25% warn/fail at 5k in / 4k out; ×3 runs | $4 | **$10–60** |
| Rationale per prioritization run | 400 targets × sol (3k / 1.5k) × ≥3 waves | $4 | **$8–25** (≈$1 on luna) |
| PM challenge | ~140 sol calls | $10 | $10 ✓ |
| **Total** | | **≈$40** | **≈$55–150** |

- **Thresholds are inconsistent** (`DECISIONS.md:117`): a hard stop at $90 leaves only **$15** of the "$25 demo reserve" usable.
- **Other gaps:**
  - The guard can't stop spend from a Batch job that's already running, so it needs to estimate and reserve the cost before submitting.
  - Batch can take up to 24h to finish, which doesn't suit hackathon pace. Flex is the same price and much faster.
  - Cache writes cost 1.25×, and Batch may get few cache hits (30-minute cache lifetime).
  - The OpenAI project hard limit is enforced (`project_spend_limit_exceeded`), but it resets monthly and can overshoot slightly. Set it to **$90**, not $100.
- **Model choice is sound:** luna is the cheapest viable model with Structured Outputs, and sol suits the reasoning steps.
  - The `gpt-5-mini` fallback costs 2.5–4× more than luna; it's fine as a quality fallback, but don't call it the cheap option.
  - Sol can't run with zero reasoning effort, so always set effort explicitly.
- **Fix:** use luna for rationale text (scoring itself is deterministic); run sol fit checks only on `fail`, once per requirement rather than per target; cap web search in calls, not requests; re-baseline the plan at ~$70 with the corrected thresholds.

---

## Important

**Data inventory (`data-inventory.md`)**
- **I1. Text length:** ":18 avg ~300 chars" is wrong; the actual figure is **213–223**.
- **I2. Source D** (`:33`, Q-005): "short answers to 'what could be improved'" is backwards. 76–83% of Source D texts use positive words versus 2–4% negative, so D looks like a "what do you like" answer.
- **I3. Source A** is multi-country (US/KR/JP/GB…) and written in normalized lowercase, which suggests translated survey text, not "online reviews".
- **I4. Q-005's guesses feed straight into trust weighting.** Mark them as hypotheses until the mentors answer.
- **I5. Study file:**
  - CN_EU means are **numeric cells, not strings** (openpyxl type `n`, format `#,##0.00`).

Euro NCAP's 2026 protocols require dedicated physical controls for turn indicators, hazard lights, windscreen wipers, the horn, and SOS/eCall functions. ETSC's January 2026 write-up reports this as part of a broader overhaul built on four pillars: Safe Driving, Crash Avoidance, Crash Protection, and Post-Crash Safety. To secure a top safety rating, manufacturers must provide dedicated physical controls for core functions, and ETSC lists the indicators, wipers, horn, and SOS/eCall functions among them.

Other outlets say the same thing with some differences in emphasis:

- **Requirement level:** One source says to earn maximum points, vehicles must include tangible controls for essential operations. Another says the controls are needed if automakers want a five-star safety rating.
- **Scope:** Euro NCAP does not require every function to have its own button. Euro NCAP is not insisting on everything being its own button or switch.
- **Enforcement:** Euro NCAP testing is voluntary, and it can't force automakers to do anything, though many manufacturers use its ratings in marketing.
- **Context:** The move targets touchscreen-heavy interiors. Euro NCAP has said that new tests set to be introduced in 2026 will aim to encourage car manufacturers to reintegrate separate, physical controls for basic functions. Tesla's steering-wheel haptic buttons for turn signals are cited as the most exposed case.

ETSC applauds the direction but argues that voluntary ratings are not a substitute for legislation.

Source note: the ETSC article is the most authoritative of these results, but the search did not return Euro NCAP's own protocol document, so the exact wording of the test criteria is not verified here.

input.content:
# Data Inventory

All raw files: `challange information document/BMW-Data/` (read-only, git-ignored). Profiled 2026-10-10; re-verified 2026-10-10 (pandas 3 in a `uv` Python 3.12 env + openpyxl/pdftotext).

**Counting rule:** the feedback files have one row per (verbatim × classification). All verbatim counts below are **unique `ID`s** unless a column says "rows".

## 1. Customer feedback (verbatims) — `{F70,G60,G70}_feedback_hackathon.xlsx`

Sheet `Feedback_Explorer`, 12 columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ID` | Verbatim ID, e.g. `G60-0001`. **Not unique per row** — one row per (verbatim × classification). An ID never spans two sources. |
| `Source` | Anonymized channel `Source A`–`D` (interpretation open, Q-005) |
| `Brand`, `Sales Description` | `[BMW]`, `[BMW 5 Series]` |
| `Country` | ISO-2 (US, GB, JP, KR, …) |
| `Derivate (e-code)` | F70 / G60 / G70 |
| `Engine Type` | `ICE`, `PHEV`, `BEVE` (= BEV; the raw value is `BEVE`) |
| `Feedback Type` | `Likes`, `Difficult to Use`, `Defect`, `Wants`, or empty (unclassified) |
| `Customer Feedback` | Free text, mean ~215–225 chars per verbatim (Source D ~125) |
| `Vfc level2 3 Name` | Combined "Component : Issue" label |
| `Vfc level2 Name` | Component / topic (e.g. `Seats`, `Touch screen, operation`, `Electric Range`) |
| `Vfc level3 Name` | Issue type (e.g. `Not user-friendly`, `Like: function`, `Customer request: function`) |

| File | Rows | Verbatims (unique IDs) | Sources (verbatims) | Countries (verbatims) | Engines (verbatims) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | 4,076 | 2,128 | A 2,128 | GB 1,293, **JP 672**, SE 71, FR 53, AU 16, FI 8, DK 8, KR 4 | ICE 2,128 |
| G60 | 5,005 | 4,000 | B 2,626, A 854, C 384, D 136 | **US 3,610 (90%)**, KR 205, JP 53, GB 36, SE 28, DK 20, CA 18, … | ICE 2,259, BEV 1,363, PHEV 378 |
| G70 | 4,690 | 4,000 | B 2,853, A 695, C 314, D 138 | **US 3,792 (95%)**, KR 137, JP 40, CA 8, GB 8, … | ICE 2,568, BEV 1,129, PHEV 303 |

European verbatims: F70 ~1,430 (67%), G60 ~110, **G70 ~19**. Row counts overstate Source A, which carries the most multi-label rows: G60 Source A has 1,858 rows but only 854 verbatims.

Quirks:
- **Dedupe by `ID`** when counting verbatims; keep all rows as classification labels.
- **Unclassified verbatims:**
  - Source A: `Feedback Type` empty ⇔ `Vfc level2 = no_class_found`. That is 300 of F70's 2,128 verbatims (14%; 27% of rows).
  - Source D: no BMW classification at all.
  - Source C: ~70 verbatims per file have an empty type *and* an empty topic.
  - → Our own LLM classification is needed; the BMW taxonomy is a hint.
- 120 (F70) / 221 (G60) / 211 (G70) distinct `Vfc level2` values incl. `no_class_found`. Top topics: Drivetrain, Handling/Riding, Body equipment, Exterior design, Seats, Touch screen, Electric Range.
- Observed text patterns per source. These are **observations, not channel identities** (Q-005):
  - **A:** all derivatives, many countries (incl. JP/KR), lower-case normalized text ("the car…", "i really…"), so possibly translated.
  - **B:** US only; most verbatims start "Customer stated / mentioned / reported / commented…" (third-person notes).
  - **C:** US only; ~40% start "I had a minor/serious problem with…", others "What is…" / "If there…" (structured survey prompts); mostly Difficult-to-Use/Defect.
  - **D:** US only; short, ~80% positive wording ("love the…"), unclassified. It looks like answers to a "what do you like" question, **not** "what could be improved".
- **No China verbatims** for any derivative. There is **no date column** — no time series possible.

## 2. Customer studies — `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx`

### Sheet `CN_EU_2025` (76 content rows; openpyxl reports 84 incl. trailing empty rows)
- Columns: China → `BMW 5 Series G68`, `BMW 7 Series G70`; EU → `BMW 1 Series F70`, `BMW 5 Series G60`, `BMW 7 Series G70`.
- 37 categories, each a label row followed by a `Mean` row. Values are **numeric cells** (format `#,##0.00`), range ~6.5–9.9. Scale unconfirmed (0–10 or 1–10?; Q-006).
- **No sample sizes.**
- Categories: overall satisfaction, exterior/interior styling, interior quality, equipment level, safety, squeaks/rattles, value for money, reliability, visibility, controls/displays, smartphone integration, infotainment features + ease of use, navigation, seating comfort, small-item storage, acceleration, roadholding, efficiency, braking, sportiness, prestige, manoeuvrability, ride quality, front/rear roominess, luggage loading + capacity, ingress/egress, environmental friendliness, HVAC, build quality, quietness, driving position, connected services, interior versatility.

### Sheet `US_2025` (929 content rows; openpyxl reports 934)
- Columns: question, `% of column, sample base`, `BMW 5 Series G60`, `BMW 7 Series G70`.
- 103 questions, each block = `Sample total` + 7-point distribution: I Hate It / A Failure / Unsatisfactory / Satisfactory / Excellent / Delightful / I Love It. Shares 0–1; every block sums to 1.0.
- **`Sample total` = 1 is the share base, not a respondent count → no sample sizes.** No significance testing or n-weighting is possible.
- Granular: exterior (proportions, wheels, door handles, lights, door sound), driving (ride, handling, power), interior (materials, seats per row, roominess, storage, cupholders, cargo), climate, audio, controls intuitiveness, NVH, …
- **No F70 in US.**
- Useful derived metrics: top-2-box (Delightful + I Love It), bottom-3-box, net score. CN/EU means and US distributions are **not directly comparable** (Q-006).

## 3. Sales volumes — `sales_volumes.xlsx`

Sheets `F70`, `G60_G68`, `G70`; columns `market, market_code, volume_2024, volume_2025, volume_2030` (2030 = forecast).

| Derivative | EU 25 | CN 25 | US 25 | RoW 25 | Total 24 → 25 → 2030 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | 85k | 0 | 0 | 28k | 105k → 113k → 118k |
| G60/G68 | 115k | 75k | 78k | 28k | 278.6k → 296k → 316k |
| G70 | 13k | 10k | 12k | 7k | 34k → 42k → 52k |

- **No powertrain split**, although `data_and_source.png` says "units by powertrain and region". Engine mix can only be inferred from feedback.
- `G60_G68` is one combined sheet, with no G60/G68 split. CN is presumably the G68 LWB.
- **Values look stylized and conflict with public data** (Q-015):
  - All values except one are round thousands.
  - G60/G68 CN is 68k → 75k (+10%) for 2024 → 2025. Public figures point the other way: 5 Series China (China-built) Jan–Nov 2025 was 107,348 per CPCA via Gasgoo, and BMW+MINI China fell 12.5% in 2025 (`competitor-landscape.md`, `portfolio-reference.md`).
  - F70 EU 85k vs. 1 Series Europe 91,931 (Dataforce; "Europe" definitions differ).
  - Until clarified, treat the file as **BMW-internal relative weights**, and surface the conflict instead of mixing both sources.

## 4. Equipment / option lists — `{F70,G60,G70}_OptionList.PDF`

- German-market price lists, **in German**, text-extractable (`pdftotext -layout` works):

  | File | PDF title | Edition | Pages |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | F70 | "BMW 1er Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 1, 28.05.2026 | 23 |
  | G60 | "BMW 5er **Limousine** Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 2, 22.06.2026 | 28 |
  | G70 | "BMW 7er Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 1, 28.05.2026 | 27 |

  The G60 list covers the sedan incl. i5 — **no Touring (G61)**.
- Sections: Fahrzeugpreise (models, power, consumption, price), Serienausstattung(en) (standard equipment per model), M Sportpaket / Pro, Räder & Reifen, Farbwelt, **Sonderausstattungen (options)**, Technische Werte.
- Matrix tables use `■` = standard; options with price.
- Use: baseline "what the car offers today", package structure, gaps vs. competitors.
- The briefing promises equipment "by trim and **market**", but only DE was provided. For US/CN it's an **assumption** that equipment is comparable.

## 5. Briefing material
- `BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf` (2 pages). **Image-only (no text layer):** `pdftotext` returns nothing, so render it (`pdftoppm`) to read it.
- `mission.md`.
- `data_and_source.png`: dataset purpose table.
- `image_1.png`: "1 billion findings → 1,000 requirements → one car" + example verbatims/themes.
- `image_2.png`: reference process.

## Coverage matrix (what we can say where)

| | EU | US | CN | RoW |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | ~1.4k verbatims (GB-heavy), study, sales | — | — | **~690 verbatims (JP 672)**, sales |
| G60/G68 | ~110 verbatims, study, sales | **~3.6k verbatims, detailed study, sales** | study (G68), sales | ~280 verbatims (KR 205, JP, CA), sales |
| G70 | ~19 verbatims (≈ none), study, sales | **~3.8k verbatims, detailed study, sales** | study, sales | ~190 verbatims (KR 137, JP), sales |

- RoW verbatims (JP/KR/CA/AU) are separate customer groups under D-011 — don't fold them into EU.
- External/web data fills gaps: competitors (Mercedes E/S/A-Class, Audi A6/e-tron, Tesla, NIO, XPeng, Li Auto, BYD…), reviews, trends.
